subject: what to do when you need to use a parameter value as an index?

messages.author: 44b550321f5c6209
messages.subject: what to do when you need to use a parameter value as an index?
parts:
Hi all,

I am working on an age-structured mark-recapture model with time- and age-specific survival and (re)capture rates. Right now, I am assuming age can be determined with certainty, so I am able to make age a data value, not a parameter. As a result, I can use age to access time- and age-specific rates--e.g. phi[t-1,age[i,t-1]]. However, there is substantial error in the ageing process, so I need to make age a parameter so I can account for its state uncertainty. Is there a workaround so I can use age as an index to call up age-specific rates even though age will now be a parameter?

Thank you!

Rebecca

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: what to do when you need to use a parameter value as an index?
parts:
Hi Rebecca,

Can you clarify a bit?  If you have age as a parameter (i.e. there is a stochastic declaration like "age[i, t] ~ dcat(...)") that should just work.  But I might not be getting the picture of what you want.

Perry

messages.subject: Re: [EXTERNAL] Re: what to do when you need to use a parameter value as an index?
parts:
Hi Perry,

Thanks for responding so quickly. Let me try again. The problem is not how to make age a parameter. The problem is how to use a parameter as an index. 

In particular, I need to be able to access a matrix of time- and age-specific rates using the parameter age[i,t].

For example, consider the 73rd individual in my data set at time 2. In any given iteration, it will have an age of "age[73,2]", and it would survive with rate "phi[2, age[73,2]]". But Nimble doesn't seem to want me to use a parameter as an index for phi. As far as I can tell, I can only use a data value or a constant as an index.

Does that make sense?

Rebecca
